newsitem.title: USA: Blizzards, bitter cold hit northern U.S. plains.
newsitem.headline: Blizzards, bitter cold hit northern U.S. plains.

text.p: One of the worst winter storms in recent memory engulfed the northern U.S. plains on Tuesday, stranding thousands in their homes amid white-out conditions and bitter cold.

Snowdrifts as deep as four feet (1.2 metres) closed highways on Monday in the Dakotas and authorities said many roads may not be reopened until Wednesday because ploughs have been unable to keep up with the drifts.
Weather was blamed for an 18-vehicle pileup in northwest Nebraska. Authorities said no serious injuries were reported in the chain-reaction crash, which happened in zero-visibility on Monday night.
Rick Robinson, supervisor of radio communications in North Dakota, said dozens of vehicles were stranded along highways but no snowplows or wreckers were going out in the blizzard.

National Weather Service Forecaster Larry Manthe said he could not remember the last time North Dakota was hit by a blizzard lasting two days and he advised residents to stay home if possible because the storm was "a killer." He said wind on Monday topped 50 mph (80 kph) in some parts of the state.
In Canada, Royal Canadian Mounted Police on Monday closed sections of the TransCanada Highway, where a dozen cars piled up. No serious injuries or deaths were reported.

The northern plains were not the only area of the country hit by severe weather. At Deer Valley Ski Resort near Park City, Utah, six judges were injured on Monday when the elevated stand they were on blew over. Officials said the injuries forced them to cancel the NorAm Amateur Freestyle skiing event.
